key_insight: Darwin-Claw turns raw agent interactions into structured, environment-specific experience prototypes so self-evolving LLM agents can adapt continuously without losing controllability.
engineering_relevance: It offers a deployable framework for building user-centric agents that improve over time through automated memory consolidation and skill refinement in real-world systems.
method: Hierarchical Experience Consolidation extracts fine-grained error attributions from episodes.
These attributions are generalized into dynamically updated prototype vectors.
The consolidated experience is reused as interaction patches and optimization signals for perception and skill updates.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive experiments on WildClawBench, with substantial performance improvements over prior approaches.
watch_item: Performance and stability likely depend on the quality of error attribution and prototype updates, so noisy interactions could still degrade consolidation.
paper_title: Darwin-Claw: Environment-Adaptive Experience Consolidation for Recursively Self-Evolving Agents
